sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Primary Objective**: To conserve water, minimize wastage, and ensure more equitable distribution both across and within states through integrated water resources development and management.
• **Climate Adaptation Focus**: NWM emphasizes **adaptation** to climate change impacts on water resources, such as glacial melt, erratic rainfall, and increased frequency of droughts/floods.
• **Institutional Framework**: NWM is implemented by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti** (formerly Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation).
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The mission targets a **20% improvement in water use efficiency** through regulatory, legislative, and fiscal measures.

items.definition: A process which promotes the coordinated development and management of water, land, and related resources to maximize economic and social welfare without compromising the sustainability of vital ecosystems.
The ratio of water used for a specific purpose to the total water withdrawn. NWM aims to increase this by 20% across industrial, agricultural, and domestic sectors.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Catch the Rain Campaign**: A 'Jan Andolan' to nudge states and stakeholders to create appropriate Rain Water Harvesting Structures (RWHS).
• **Atal Bhujal Yojana**: A central sector scheme for sustainable management of groundwater with community participation.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Fragmented institutional responsibility, lack of real-time data, and over-extraction of groundwater for agriculture.
• **Solutions**: Implementation of the National Water Framework Bill, incentivizing micro-irrigation (PMKSY), and decentralized water governance.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'D-A-T-A-S'
• **Decoded Meaning**: D-atabase (National), A-daptation (Climate), T-echnology (Efficiency), A-wareness (Jan Andolan), S-ustainable (Groundwater management).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses NWM with the 'Jal Jeevan Mission'. Remember: NWM is a policy-level mission under NAPCC (Climate Change), while Jal Jeevan Mission is an infrastructure-delivery mission (Har Ghar Jal).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Hydro-climatic resilience' when discussing NWM in the context of climate change adaptation.

keyTakeaways: NWM is one of the 8 missions under NAPCC, focusing on climate adaptation.
The core target is a 20% increase in water use efficiency.
It emphasizes decentralized, community-led water management (Jan Andolan).
